title: The machine keeps going
caption: A spring helper moves the point, moves its own base, catches its sleeve and leaves the student with an event to watch.
connection: Diakur's combination of puppeteering and dynamic simulation suggests a way to direct an attempt while letting its body complicate the action.
lesson: Carry the spring and familiar sphere forward. Compare a fixed base with a rolling base. Observe what continues after release.
question: When does correcting the demonstration become part of the comedy?

title: A room with other plans
caption: Three agents approach one point. Their movement creates a blockage, shifts a partition and leaves an unplanned gathering.
connection: Ritual's responsive inhabitants suggest a room where the visitor is one participant among others. This new scene uses Ada's own proposed objects.
lesson: Reuse a simple approach rule and contact. Let another body alter the route. Inspect which outcome belongs to the rule and which to their interaction.
question: Does every body have to finish its assigned task for the encounter to matter?

title: The body carries its history
caption: The black point acquires parts. Weight, wind and contact turn its added uses into a strange material arrangement.
connection: Torn's assemblages of consumer and internet remains suggest attachments with histories. Our extension asks what those parts do to a body's balance and relations.
lesson: Retain the point and change its attachments. Compare where a force acts, what bears the load and which surfaces become support.
question: Where does the object end once its accessories become conditions of its movement?
